title: FuXi-γ: Efficient Sequential Recommendation with Exponential-Power Temporal Encoder and Diagonal-Sparse Positional Mechanism

problem.claim: Sequential recommendation must model users' evolving preferences from historical interactions.

gap.claim: Transformer-based sequential recommenders can incur high computational overhead from discontinuous memory access in temporal encoding and dense attention over long sequences.

contributions.claim: FuXi-γ is a sequential recommendation framework designed to improve effectiveness and efficiency through architectural design.

The exponential-power temporal encoder models relative temporal intervals with a tunable exponential decay function, supporting short-term and long-term preference modeling through continuous memory access and matrix operations.
The diagonal-sparse positional mechanism prunes low-contribution attention blocks with a diagonal-sliding strategy guided by Toeplitz-matrix persymmetry.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present FuXi-γ as a novel framework with two key architectural innovations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art recommendation quality on four real-world datasets.
The authors report training acceleration of up to 4.74× and inference acceleration of up to 6.18×.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation models users' evolving preferences from historical interactions.
Transformer-based approaches capture global dependencies but face computational overhead on temporal encoding and long-sequence attention.
FuXi-γ is proposed to improve recommendation effectiveness and efficiency.
The framework combines an exponential-power temporal encoder with a diagonal-sparse positional mechanism.
Experiments on four real-world datasets are reported to show strong recommendation quality and faster training and inference.

source_observation.claim: The method represents temporal intervals with a tunable exponential decay and uses continuous memory access and pure matrix operations.

interpretation.claim: Temporal modeling may be made more efficient when its computation is expressed through regular matrix operations while retaining adjustable recency sensitivity.

application.claim: Consider continuous, matrix-friendly temporal encodings when sequence models need both recency sensitivity and computational efficiency.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this tradeoff holds across domains, sequence lengths, or temporal distributions beyond the reported datasets.

source_observation.claim: The positional mechanism prunes low-contribution attention blocks using a diagonal-sliding strategy.

interpretation.claim: Structured sparsity guided by positional or matrix properties may reduce long-sequence attention cost while preserving selected interactions.

application.claim: Use structured attention sparsification when long sequences make dense attention prohibitively expensive.

exception.claim: The abstract does not quantify the quality or efficiency tradeoff caused by pruning individual attention blocks.

unknowns: The four datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, and experimental settings are unspecified.
Ablation results and the separate effects of the two architectural components are unspecified.
The source does not establish independent verification of the reported performance or speedups.
